crossCheckedAgainst: src/data/taxonomy.json (248 registry rows; all 50 rows diffed field-by-field against their record)
src/data/levels.json (17 anchors; every record's levels[] tested against its own extent)
src/assets/anatomy/anatomy-manifest.json (138 committed parts; bbox/centroid used as frozen ground truth)
src/data/syndromes/diencephalon.json (7 cards; every diencephalic record's clinical claim cross-read)
src/geometry/anatomyAssets.ts (LINKS) + src/components/viewer3d/SceneLayers.tsx (SLOTS) for which records own a committed body
src/data/plates.json (15 manifests; the plate tags asserted in the records' own contextNote fields)
scope.notAuditedHere: tracts.json, syndromes/* as records, plates/*.svg label geometry, midbrain/pons/medulla records, vasculature.json (owned by the other phase-1 auditors); anatomyAssets.ts/SceneLayers.tsx source is read-only evidence, not an audited artifact

method.probes: read + node one-liners over the JSON, the manifest and the registry; no gate was run except `npm run validate` (0 errors / 0 warnings); no browser lane, no re-bake, no src/** write
method.positionTolerance: origin3d is a marker; for records that own a committed body the mesh bbox is the ground truth and a marker/mesh centroid offset of up to ~3 au in y/z is the documented placement convention (measured across this file), so it is NOT reported; the x offset on paired records is deliberate (the committed sculpts are bilateral, the marker sits on one side). size3d is only audited where the record has no committed body (per the plan's C4).

findings.claimed: "Interventricular foramen (of Monro) from the third ventricle — CSF inflow and the route by which intraventricular pressure is transmitted"
findings.expected: CSF leaves the lateral ventricle through the interventricular foramen INTO the third ventricle; nothing flows from the third ventricle into the lateral ventricle. The afferent/efferent direction is inverted.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction: `vent-third-ventricle.connections.afferent` says "Lateral ventricles via the interventricular foramina of Monro" and `vent-interventricular-foramen.connections` says afferent = "Anterior part of the lateral ventricle (frontal horn and body)", efferent = "Third ventricle" — both siblings state the correct direction for the same CSF route. Standard anatomy (Blumenfeld, Brain and Environs: Cranium, Ventricles, and Meninges) agrees with the siblings.
findings.suggestedFix: Rewrite the afferent/efferent pair as: afferent — "Choroid plexus of the lateral ventricle (production)"; efferent — "Interventricular foramen of Monro → third ventricle → cerebral aqueduct → fourth ventricle". Keep the venous-drainage sentence as a separate efferent item.
findings.notes: This is the parent record of the ventricular group and the wrong direction propagates to six sibling records (dienc-002…dienc-008). Fix the root text first, then the siblings.

findings.claimed: "It receives CSF from the third ventricle through the interventricular foramen, hosts the choroid plexus that produces most of it, and drains through the atrium into the temporal horn and thence to the fourth ventricle"
findings.expected: "It hosts the choroid plexus that produces most of the CSF and drains through the interventricular foramen into the third ventricle, and thence through the aqueduct to the fourth ventricle." The lateral ventricle does not receive CSF from the third ventricle, and the temporal horn is a blind posterior/inferior recess — there is no temporal-horn → fourth-ventricle route.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with `vent-third-ventricle.function` ("the interventricular foramina of Monro drain both lateral ventricles into it") and with the record's own segment records; standard CSF-flow anatomy (Blumenfeld, same chapter).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the drainage clause with the foramen → third ventricle → aqueduct → fourth ventricle route; state that the temporal horn carries no outflow.
findings.notes: The same wrong route is repeated in the body, atrium, temporal-horn and occipital-horn records.

findings.claimed: afferent[0] "Interventricular foramen (of Monro) at its posterior floor, from the third ventricle"; afferent[1] "CSF secreted by the choroid plexus of the body, which begins behind the foramen"
findings.expected: The foramen is the OUTFLOW of the frontal horn (frontal horn/body → foramen → third ventricle); the choroid plexus of the body does not deliver CSF forward into the horn (it has no plexus of its own).
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with `vent-interventricular-foramen.connections` (which puts the lateral ventricle on the afferent side) and with `vent-choroid-plexus-lateral.function` ("absent from the frontal and occipital horns"); standard CSF-flow anatomy.
findings.suggestedFix: afferent — "None; the horn is a blind anterior recess with no choroid plexus"; efferent — "Continuous posteriorly with the body, then the interventricular foramen → third ventricle".
findings.notes: The record's own functional paragraph is otherwise correct (caudate head laterally, septum pellucidum medially, cornu anterius / Evans index).

findings.claimed: afferent[0] "Interventricular foramen … anteriorly — CSF arriving from the third ventricle and from the frontal horn"; efferent[0] "Atrium … posteriorly, then the temporal horn, the cerebral aqueduct and the fourth ventricle"
findings.expected: CSF in the body flows anteriorly to the foramen of Monro and out into the third ventricle; the posterior route (atrium → temporal horn) is a dead end and never reaches the aqueduct. The aqueduct is reached from the third ventricle, not from the atrium.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with `vent-third-ventricle.connections.efferent` ("Cerebral aqueduct (to the fourth ventricle)" is downstream of the third ventricle, not of the atrium) and with the sibling foramen record; standard CSF-flow anatomy.
findings.suggestedFix: afferent — "Choroid plexus of the body (production); the frontal horn anteriorly"; efferent — "Interventricular foramen anteriorly → third ventricle → aqueduct → fourth ventricle; the atrium/temporal horn are blind posterior recesses".
findings.notes: The rest of the record (thalamostriate groove, venous angle, central neurocytoma, Evans/index context) is accurate.

findings.claimed: afferent[0] "Atrium (drains the body and occipital horn) — the temporal horn is the CSF exit route toward the fourth ventricle"; efferent[0] "CSF flows posteriorly from the temporal horn through the atrium to the cerebral aqueduct"
findings.expected: The temporal horn is a blind forward-curving recess: CSF enters it from the atrium and leaves it only by the same route. It is not an exit route to the fourth ventricle, and no CSF path runs atrium → aqueduct.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the sibling records (dienc-001/003/004) and with `vent-third-ventricle`; standard anatomy — the lateral ventricle communicates with the third ventricle only through the foramen of Monro.
findings.suggestedFix: afferent — "Atrium (trigone), with the choroid plexus entering along the choroidal fissure"; efferent — "Back to the atrium; the horn is the terminal recess of the lateral ventricle".
findings.notes: The anatomical description of the horn's walls (caudate tail and tapetum in the roof, hippocampus and fimbria in the floor/medial wall) is correct.

findings.claimed: afferent[0] "Atrium (trigone) — CSF arriving from the body and from the temporal horn"; efferent[0] "CSF returns to the atrium and then to the cerebral aqueduct and fourth ventricle; the horn is a blind posterior recess"
findings.expected: No CSF arrives from the temporal horn (that horn is a terminal recess, not a conduit), and the aqueduct is not reached from the atrium. The afferent must be just the atrium.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction: the record's own efferent sentence says the horn is a blind recess, which is incompatible with its afferent sentence receiving flow from the temporal horn; and the atrium → aqueduct link contradicts `vent-third-ventricle.connections.efferent`.
findings.suggestedFix: afferent — "Atrium (trigone)"; efferent — "None; blind posterior recess — CSF returns to the atrium and leaves the ventricle only through the foramen of Monro".
findings.notes: The horn's wall description (tapetum roof, calcar avis and bulb medially, collateral trigone laterally) matches Gray's/Blumenfeld and is left unchanged.

findings.claimed: "CSF leaves through the temporal horn toward the fourth ventricle; the plexus at the glomus absorbs and produces CSF and is the landmark for atrial surgery"
findings.expected: "CSF leaves through the foramen of Monro via the body (with the temporal and occipital horns as terminal recesses); the glomus absorbs and produces CSF and is the surgical landmark."
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with `vent-third-ventricle`/`vent-interventricular-foramen`; standard anatomy. A temporal horn has no outlet to the fourth ventricle.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the temporal-horn → fourth-ventricle clause and state the foramen-of-Monro route.
findings.notes: The glomus/plexus content and the atrial-surgery clinical items are unaffected.

findings.claimed: "CSF secreted into the lateral ventricles flows through the interventricular foramen to the third ventricle (and, from the atrium and temporal horn, posteriorly toward the aqueduct)"
findings.expected: The route is lateral ventricle → foramen of Monro → third ventricle → aqueduct; there is no atrial/temporal route to the aqueduct.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with `vent-third-ventricle`; standard anatomy. The first clause of the same sentence is correct, so only the parenthetical is defective.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the parenthetical, or replace it with "the atrium and temporal horn are the plexus-bearing terminal segments of that same lateral-ventricle compartment".
findings.notes: The record's extension (foramen → body → atrium → temporal horn, absent from the frontal and occipital horns) and its blood supply are correct.

findings.claimed: laterality "midline", origin3d [0, 28.5, 0.5], size3d [4.5, 5.5, 5.5]
findings.expected: laterality "paired". The internal medullary lamina is a Y-shaped sheet inside EACH thalamus; at x = 0 the record's marker is centred in the third ventricle (whose committed mesh spans x −1.1…1.0), not in either thalamus. With no committed body this record draws its v1 ellipsoid from size3d at origin3d (NucleusMesh.tsx:184), so a 9 x 11 x 11 au blob is drawn astride the midline.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own function sentence ("partitions the thalamus into anterior, medial and lateral nuclear masses") and with every sibling thalamic record, which are paired and offset laterally (nuc-thalamic-reticular x = 11.5, nuc-vl 8.5, nuc-lateral-dorsal 5.5); standard anatomy (TA/FMA: lamina medullaris interna thalami, one per thalamus).
findings.suggestedFix: Set laterality "paired" and place the marker in one thalamus, e.g. origin3d [6.5, 28.5, 0.5] with size3d reduced to a lamina-plausible marker (the sheet is a few mm thick, ~[1.2, 4.0, 4.5]); the plate tags (plate-thalamus-mid, plate-coronal-thalamus) and levels[] are unaffected.
findings.notes: This is the one real midline/paired error in the 50 records (the sign contract itself is clean, as the plan's C5 measured). nuc-midline-thalamic, nuc-preoptic, vent-third-ventricle, vent-cerebral-aqueduct, tract-posterior-commissure and the pineal records are legitimately midline and were left alone.

findings.expected: Must agree with the committed chiasm geometry. ctx-optic-chiasm-l/r measure x −6.1…6.3, y 10.4…18.6, z 14.3…23.5 and the committed tract-optic-nerve waypoints end at [2, 23.5, 23.5]; the record is 5.5 au above and 13.5 au behind that chain. Either this record moves to the baked chiasm (≈[0, 16, 20]) or the record is declared authoritative and the v8 optic chain is re-fitted — they cannot both stand.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with a committed mesh bbox + a sibling record: `ctx-optic-chiasm` (telencephalon-optic-pathway.json) is [0, 23.5, 23.5] for the same structure — two registered records for one chiasm, Δy 5.5 au and Δz 13.5 au (14.6 au Euclidean). PLAN.md §2.7 measured this divergence ("6–10 au") and §8.2 already concluded "Fixing that record, not the path, is the right follow-up". Note the anatomical cost of that fix: the record's own y = 29 is 1 au from the mammillary-body mesh centre (28.0) and sits correctly rostral to the infundibulum (z 7), whereas y ≈ 16 would put the chiasm at the level of the superior colliculus (lvl-midbrain-sc, y 14).
findings.suggestedFix: Reconcile the two chiasm records with the frozen optic geometry and pick ONE authority. If the record is moved to the mesh, do it together with dienc-011 (its level) and flag the resulting conflict with surf-infundibulum [0,27,7]; if the record is kept, the divergence must be recorded in contextNote as a known, frozen misregistration instead of being silently contradicted by ctx-optic-chiasm.
findings.notes: Reported by this audit because surf-optic-chiasm is authored in diencephalon-hypothalamus.json; ctx-optic-chiasm itself is in the telencephalon auditor's set and is cited here only as the contradicting sibling. CN II's tube (src/geometry/curves.ts) already follows the committed waypoints, not this record, so today the atlas draws a chiasm that disagrees with its own landmark record.

findings.claimed: ["lvl-thalamus-rostral"]
findings.expected: ["lvl-thalamus-mid"] on the record's own coordinates (y = 29 vs the mid-thalamus anchor 28), or whatever level the integrator re-anchors after dienc-010/dienc-012 is settled. The claimed level (y = +36) intersects neither the record's marker extent (y 28.0…30.0) nor the committed chiasm mesh (y 10.4…18.6).
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with src/data/levels.json:14 (lvl-thalamus-rostral y = +36) plus the record's own origin3d; the level is the only one in the table named for a structure ("… (optic chiasm)") that does not contain that structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Couple this edit to dienc-010: whichever way the chiasm's position is resolved, make its levels[] name the plane that actually passes through it.
findings.notes: The same asymmetry applies to nuc-supraoptic (y = 30, mesh 27.8…29.4) and nuc-suprachiasmatic (y = 31, mesh 27.8…29.4), which also list only lvl-thalamus-rostral; if the level anchor is moved (dienc-012) they inherit the fix, otherwise give them lvl-thalamus-mid as well.

findings.claimed: y = 36, name "Diencephalon — rostral thalamus / hypothalamus (optic chiasm)"
findings.expected: The anchor and/or the name must match the structures that claim this level. Every other level in the table is anchored on the landmark it names (lvl-thalamus-mid y = 28 = the mammillary-body mesh centroid 28.0; lvl-midbrain-sc y = 14 = nuc-superior-colliculus origin3d y 14; lvl-midbrain-ic y = 8 = nuc-inferior-colliculus y 8; lvl-post-comm y = 19 ≈ tract-posterior-commissure y 20). This one names the optic chiasm, but the chiasm's record is at y = 29, its sibling record at y = 23.5 and its committed mesh at y 10.4…18.6 — so nothing named there is at +36.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction across three authored artifacts (levels.json, the two chiasm records, the mesh bbox) plus the table's own demonstrated anchor convention. The structures that DO sit at +36 are the rostral hypothalamic group (nuc-paraventricular y 35.5, nuc-preoptic 34, nuc-dorsomedial 34), all of which list this level.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) rename the level to "Diencephalon — rostral hypothalamus (paraventricular/preoptic)" and keep y = +36 (lowest risk: no coordinate moves, no plate uses this level — the 10 transverse plates anchor on thalamus-mid, the three midbrain levels, four pontine/medullary levels and tel-basal-ganglia), or (b) move the anchor to ≈ +30 and re-check the six records whose levels[] contain it. Do not move the anchor without (a)/(b) reconciliation, because the optic-chiasm name would then be wrong in a different way.
findings.notes: levels.json is not a structure record, but it is the anchor table the dispatch asked this auditor to test the level[] sets against, and the integrator owns src/data/**.

findings.expected: The defining relation (medial geniculate body ventral AND medial to the lateral geniculate body) should be unambiguous. The record expresses the medial offset correctly (x 8 vs 11) but only 0.5 au (0.6 mm) of vertical offset, so the two markers overlap in y; the committed meshes put the MGN centroid (y 22.1) ABOVE the LGN centroid (y 21.2). Anatomy puts the MGB clearly below the LGB (roughly 3–5 mm).
findings.basis: Mesh bbox cross-check (MGN y 20.7…24.5 vs LGN y 11.7…31.1 — the oversized LGN sculpt cannot resolve the pair) plus textbook anatomy (Fix, Neuroanatomy: the medial geniculate body lies inferior and medial to the lateral geniculate body, below the pulvinar).
findings.suggestedFix: Lower the MGN marker to y ≈ 20.5–21 (still inside its own committed mesh, y 20.7…24.5) so the pair reads as MGN-below-LGN; leave z and x. Do NOT ask for a mesh change — the meshes are frozen.
findings.notes: Direction is right, magnitude is not expressed; filed as a suspicion rather than a defect because a 0.5 au difference is at the limit of the marker convention used elsewhere in this file.

findings.claimed: "PCA — thalamogeniculate artery and lateral posterior choroidal artery; angular (MCA) branches supply the lateral pole."
findings.expected: "PCA — thalamogeniculate artery and lateral posterior choroidal artery (the whole pulvinar is PCA territory)." The middle cerebral artery never supplies the thalamus; its angular branches supply the parietal association cortex, not the lateral pulvinar.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own clinical items (both attribute pulvinar lesions to PCA branches only) and with the other thalamic records in the same file (tuberothalamic / paramedian / thalamogeniculate / posterior choroidal, all PCA); standard vascular anatomy (Blumenfeld, Cerebral Hemispheres and Vascular Supply — the thalamic territories are PCA perforators plus the anterior choroidal artery).
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the angular/MCA clause; if a lateral contribution is wanted, name the anterior choroidal artery, which is the only non-PCA supply of the thalamus.
findings.notes: The record's function, connections and both clinical items are correct; only this clause invents a non-existent supply.

findings.claimed: "Prion degeneration targeting anterior and reticular thalamic nuclei abolishes sleep spindles and normal sleep architecture"
findings.expected: Fatal familial insomnia is defined by neuronal loss and gliosis of the anteroventral (AV) and mediodorsal (MD) thalamic nuclei (with the inferior olivary nucleus); the reticular nucleus is not the reported target. Suggested: "Prion degeneration targeting the anteroventral and mediodorsal thalamic nuclei abolishes sleep spindles and normal sleep architecture".
findings.basis: Own anatomical knowledge, labelled as such (FFI neuropathology: AV + MD + inferior olive; the spindle-generation mechanism the record describes does involve the reticular nucleus, which is why the two are easily conflated). No conflicting record exists in the atlas to arbitrate.
findings.suggestedFix: Name AV and MD as the degenerating nuclei; keep the TRN only in the mechanism clause ("the spindles the reticular nucleus helps generate are lost").
findings.notes: The absence-epilepsy item (T-type calcium channels, ethosuximide) is correct and unchanged.

findings.claimed: name "Centromedian-parafascicular nuclei"; synonyms ["CM-PF", "intralaminar nuclei", "centromedian nucleus", "parafascicular nucleus"]
findings.expected: The synonyms claim the whole intralaminar group for a record that covers only its caudal pair. The rostral intralaminar group (central lateral, paracentral, central medial) — and in particular the central lateral nucleus, the main intralaminar contributor to the ascending arousal system the record's function paragraph describes — is not represented anywhere in the atlas. Either widen the record or narrow the synonym.
findings.basis: Standard nomenclature (Terminologia Anatomica / FMA: the intralaminar nuclei comprise a rostral and a caudal group; CM and PF are only the caudal pair) plus the record's own text, which assigns the ARAS role to "parafascicular — with the midline nuclei" while omitting CL.
findings.suggestedFix: Either retitle to "Intralaminar nuclei (centromedian and parafascicular)" and keep the synonym, or drop "intralaminar nuclei" from the synonyms and add central lateral to the function text. The plate label already reads "CM-PF (intralaminar)" (plate-thalamus-mid), so no plate slug changes either way.
findings.notes: region/subdivision/kind/laterality and the level set are correct; the plate label is consistent with either fix.

findings.claimed: "Lateral segment of the globus pallidus externa (indirect pathway)" and "Reciprocal projections back to the globus pallidus externa"
findings.expected: "globus pallidus externus" (or the atlas's own display name "Globus pallidus, external segment" / GPe). "externa" is the feminine form that belongs with "pars externa", not with the masculine "globus pallidus".
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the atlas's canonical row `nuc-globus-pallidus-externus` (name "Globus pallidus, external segment", synonyms ["GPe", "external pallidal segment", "globus pallidus lateralis"]) and with telencephalon-basal-ganglia.json, which writes "globus pallidus internus … and externus"; standard nomenclature (TA: globus pallidus, pars externa / nucleus pallidus externus).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace both occurrences with "globus pallidus externus (GPe)".
findings.notes: The same slip occurs once in ctx-caudate-nucleus (dienc-018); it appears only in this one file, so the fix is contained.

findings.claimed: "Caudate projections to the globus pallidus externa and substantia nigra pars reticulata (indirect pathway entry)"
findings.expected: "globus pallidus externus".
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with `nuc-globus-pallidus-externus` and with telencephalon-basal-ganglia.json; standard nomenclature.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace "externa" with "externus (GPe)" — and note that the caudate's striatopallidal target is the GPe via the indirect route while its striatonigral target is the SNr, which the sentence already states correctly.
findings.notes: Filed separately from dienc-017 because it is a different record the integrator must edit.

findings.claimed: "Fields of Forel (H1/H2)" with synonyms ["thalamic fasciculus (H1)", "lenticular fasciculus (H2)"]
findings.expected: The fields of Forel are conventionally three: H1 (thalamic fasciculus), H2 (lenticular fasciculus) and H3 (the prerubral field / field H of Forel, into which the ansa lenticularis turns before joining H1). Naming the record "H1/H2" presents the complex as two fields.
findings.basis: Standard nomenclature (the H1/H2/H3 fields of Forel; TA does not enumerate them, so the definitional texts — Blumenfeld's Basal Ganglia chapter, which this record cites, and functional-neurosurgery atlases — govern) labelled as own knowledge.
findings.suggestedFix: Retitle to "Fields of Forel (H1/H2/H3)" and add H3 (prerubral field) to the contextNote, or keep the title and state explicitly that H3 is not covered.
findings.notes: The record's H1/H2 content itself is correct: H2 carries pallidal output looping through the internal capsule and H1 delivers it to VA/VL, shared with cerebellothalamic fibres.

findings.claimed: "median preoptic nucleus"
findings.expected: The median preoptic nucleus (MnPO) is one component of the preoptic area, not a synonym for it. Either drop it or qualify it ("preoptic area (median preoptic, ventrolateral preoptic and sexually dimorphic nuclei)").
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the record's own function sentence, which names "the median preoptic, ventrolateral preoptic and sexually dimorphic nuclei" as three separate constituents of the area it defines.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete "median preoptic nucleus" from synonyms; the name "Preoptic area" and the synonym "preoptic region" already cover the search index.
findings.notes: Search reads the registry row (load.ts:419-433), and the registry row carries the same synonym, so both must change together or the record/registry drift widens.

findings.claimed: "feeding center"
findings.expected: The classical "feeding centre" of the hypothalamus is the lateral hypothalamic area (with the ventromedial nucleus as the "satiety centre" — which this atlas assigns correctly in nuc-ventromedial). The arcuate (infundibular) nucleus is the source of the orexigenic NPY/AgRP and anorexigenic POMC/CART populations, not the classical feeding centre.
findings.basis: Standard physiology/functional anatomy (the lateral hypothalamic "feeding centre" vs ventromedial "satiety centre" pair), labelled as own knowledge; the atlas has no lateral-hypothalamic record that this synonym could legitimately point to.
findings.suggestedFix: Drop "feeding center" from synonyms (keep "infundibular nucleus"), or rename it "orexigenic NPY/AgRP centre" in the function text only.
findings.notes: The record's function paragraph (leptin/ghrelin/insulin sensing, GHRH and tuberoinfundibular dopamine) is accurate and unchanged.

findings.claimed: "lateral hypothalamic area (caudal)"
findings.expected: The posterior hypothalamic nucleus (posterior periventricular/medial cell group, containing the tuberomammillary histaminergic neurons the record describes) and the lateral hypothalamic area (orexin/MCH longitudinal zone) are distinct structures; listing the LHA as a synonym merges them, and no other record in the atlas defines the LHA.
findings.basis: Standard nomenclature and topography of the hypothalamic zones (medial/periventricular vs lateral longitudinal zone; TA/FMA treat them as separate entities), labelled as own knowledge, with the record's own text as corroboration (it describes a medial periventricular arousal/thermoregulatory nucleus, not the LHA).
findings.suggestedFix: Drop the synonym, or replace it with "posterior hypothalamic area" / "caudal periventricular hypothalamus".
findings.notes: Its three clinical items (heat conservation failure, Kleine-Levin-type hypersomnia, Shapiro-pattern episodic hypothermia) are all hedged appropriately and were left unchanged.

findings.claimed: ["lateral ventricle (body)", "ventriculus lateralis", "paracoele"]
findings.expected: The first synonym conflates the whole ventricle with one of its segments — and the atlas has a dedicated `vent-lateral-ventricle-body` record whose own synonyms include "pars centralis ventriculi lateralis". The search index therefore returns the whole ventricle for a query about its body.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the sibling record `vent-lateral-ventricle-body` (name "Body of the lateral ventricle") in the same subdivision; search reads the registry synonyms (load.ts:419-433).
findings.suggestedFix: Replace "lateral ventricle (body)" with "ventriculus lateralis" only, and let the five segment records own the segment names.
findings.notes: "paracoele" could not be verified against TA/FMA here (no external source consulted) — reported as unverifiable rather than wrong: the third synonym is not asserted to be an error. Deeper check: whether the whole-ventricle record needs a `(body)`-style disambiguator at all.

findings.claimed: taxonomy.json row: ["central part of the lateral ventricle", "pars centralis ventriculi lateralis"]; the record carries a third: "cellula media"
findings.expected: The registry row and the record must agree: either both carry "cellula media" or neither does. As it stands the synonym is unreachable — the search index reads the REGISTRY (load.ts:419-433), not the structure record.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between two authored files (structures/telencephalon-ventricle-segments.json vs taxonomy.json); validate-data.mjs cross-checks only `name` and `color` between the two (lines 445/452), so this drift is unchecked.
findings.suggestedFix: Sync the registry row to the record (add "cellula media") — or delete it from the record if the older term is not wanted. This is the only registry/record field drift in the 50 audited records.
findings.notes: The same audit found four contextNote drifts in the same direction (registry has extra sentences) and one in the other (ctx-pineal); see dienc-025 and the .md §5.

findings.claimed: "not a nucleus record (see the 15 individual thalamic nucleus records)"
findings.expected: "…(see the 14 individual thalamic nucleus records)" — the file holds 16 records: 14 with kind "nucleus" plus two context records (this envelope and ctx-internal-medullary-lamina). Calling the 15 non-envelope records "nucleus records" also contradicts the lamina record, whose own kind is "context" and whose text says "not a functional nucleus".
findings.basis: Internal contradiction with the file's own contents (counted: 14 nucleus-kind records) and with ctx-internal-medullary-lamina.kind.
findings.suggestedFix: Say 14; and note that the registry row for this id also carries extra text the record lacks ("3D representation: the paired GLB silhouettes ctx-thalamus-l and ctx-thalamus-r … both slots select this id") — syncing the two is worth doing in the same edit.
findings.notes: Never displayed as a count anywhere else; the mesh pairing itself (paired laterality, two slots in SceneLayers.tsx:319-320) is correct.

findings.claimed: "Hippocampal formation via the circuit of Papez (fornix, subiculum)"
findings.expected: The defining and uncontested afferent is the mammillary body via the mammillothalamic tract (which the record also lists). A DIRECT hippocampo-anterior-thalamic projection (fornix/subiculum → ANT, bypassing the mammillary bodies) is documented in rodents and debated in primates, so it should not be listed beside the mammillothalamic relay as an equal afferent — the record's own function sentence correctly routes the hippocampal signal THROUGH the mammillary bodies.
findings.basis: Own anatomical knowledge, labelled as such; internal corroboration from the record's own function sentence ("receives hippocampal information via the mammillary bodies (mammillothalamic tract)") and from nuc-mammillary-body.connections.
findings.suggestedFix: Either delete the item or qualify it: "Indirect hippocampal input via the mammillary bodies (mammillothalamic tract); a minor direct subicular projection to the anterior nuclei is described experimentally but is not the defining route."
findings.notes: The rest of the afferent/efferent set and both clinical items (tuberothalamic syndrome, Korsakoff) are correct.

findings.claimed: "GnRH neurons generate the reproductive hormone pulse"
findings.expected: The GnRH pulse generator is currently attributed to the arcuate KNDy (kisspeptin/neurokinin B/dynorphin) network, which drives the scattered preoptic/mediobasal GnRH neurons that provide the output; attributing pulse generation to the preoptic GnRH neurons themselves is the older simplification and is contested.
findings.basis: Own anatomical/neuroendocrine knowledge, labelled as such; internal corroboration is negative — nuc-arcuate-hypothalamic.efferent lists only GHRH and tuberoinfundibular dopamine for the median eminence, so the pulse generator is missing from the record that should own it.
findings.suggestedFix: Reword to "GnRH neurons of the preoptic/mediobasal hypothalamus provide the output of the reproductive hormone pulse, generated by the arcuate KNDy network" and add kisspeptin/KNDy to nuc-arcuate-hypothalamic's efferent list.
findings.notes: The thermoregulatory (warm-sensitive → heat defence) and sleep-promoting (VLPO → tuberomammillary/locus coeruleus) claims in the same sentence are correct.

findings.claimed: "retinohypothalamic glutamate/melanopsin input entrains an intrinsic ~24-hour transcriptional clock (BMAL1/CLOCK)"
findings.expected: "retinohypothalamic glutamatergic (and PACAP co-transmitter) input from melanopsin-containing retinal ganglion cells entrains…". Melanopsin is the photopigment of the ipRGCs, not a synaptic signal, so "glutamate/melanopsin input" mixes a neurotransmitter with a photopigment and omits PACAP.
findings.basis: Own knowledge of the retinohypothalamic pathway, labelled as such (RHT transmitter = glutamate with PACAP; melanopsin = the ipRGC photopigment); no conflicting record in the atlas.
findings.suggestedFix: One-clause edit, as above.
findings.notes: The rest of the record (BMAL1/CLOCK, SCN → PVN → IML → superior cervical ganglion → pineal, dorsomedial relay) is correct and consistent with nuc-pineal-gland and nuc-dorsomedial.

findings.claimed: "the atrium is the segment of the lateral-ventricle cast between the splitter planes z = −6 … and z = −24 … and above y = +22, reproducing the segment's extent y 11.2…54.6, z −23.9…−6"
findings.expected: Self-consistent numbers. A segment defined as lying ABOVE y = +22 cannot have y-min 11.2 (10.8 au below its own plane), and the sibling temporal-horn record defines itself as everything BELOW y = +22 — so the two documented extents overlap in y 11.2…22 and in z −23.9…−6, which a single splitter plane cannot produce. In the shipped geometry NO cast split exists at all (no vent-*-horn GLB part in the 138-part manifest and no splitter in scripts/build-anatomy-geometry.mjs), so these numbers are documentation of an authoring convention that the product does not implement.
findings.basis: Internal contradiction between two numbers inside the same field (the splitter-plane clause and the measured-extent clause) and between this record's extent and `vent-lateral-ventricle-temporal-horn.contextNote`.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-measure and restate: either the atrium keeps the sub-y=22 tail (then the splitter rule is not "above y = +22" but "posterior to the temporal horn") or the extent is wrong. Couple the edit with dienc-030 and say plainly that no GLB split is committed.
findings.notes: CONTENT_INVENTORY.md §11.7 states the same "above y = +22" rule, so the doc and the record share the error — fix both or neither. No geometry depends on these numbers today.

findings.claimed: six-layer retinotopic map "(ipsilateral eye 2/3/5, contralateral 1/4/6)", magnocellular motion / parvocellular form and colour / koniocellular blue-yellow, forwarding to V1 via the retrolenticular internal capsule, with the pupillary reflex spared because the pretectal fibres leave the tract before the LGN

Cross-checked for contradiction against the other optic-pathway records: nuc-pulvinar and nuc-mgn make no conflicting claim.

findings.notes: The record's clinical claims (anterior choroidal wedge sectoranopia vs lateral posterior choroidal complementary pattern; incongruous hemianopia with a spared light reflex) are also standard and were verified against the syndrome cards, which do not contradict them.
